sentences.text: The skull of Besanosaurus is dominated by a very long, thin snout that contains small teeth.
The lower jaw is primarily formed by long, thin dentary bones that bear teeth.
This animal had an elongate body shape resembling Cymbospondylus.
The holotype specimen contains 201 vertebrae, with 61 positioned before the hips.
The hindlimbs are approximately 70% the length of its forelimbs.
The largest known specimen, PIMUZ T 4847, was estimated at 8 meters long, making it the largest known ichthyosaur in its environment.
Besanosaurus is the earliest known long-snouted diapsid reptile to reach a large body size.
In 2023, researchers interpreted the embryo found in the holotype as being oriented to be born tail first, similar to merriamosaurs.
The genus Besanosaurus was named by Cristiano Dal Sasso and Giovanni Pinna in 1996.
Besanosaurus is an extinct genus of ichthyosaur found in the Monte San Giorgio region of Italy and Switzerland.
All definite specimens of Besanosaurus originate from the Besano Formation.
Paleontological work at the Sasso Caldo site on the Italian side of Monte San Giorgio began in 1985.
Dal Sasso and Pinna designated the specimen as the holotype of the new genus and species Besanosaurus leptorhynchus due to its differences from other shastasaurs.
The holotype of Besanosaurus was not the first shastasaurid specimen discovered in Monte San Giorgio.
Strong jaw muscles and a delicate snout suggest Besanosaurus fed on small fish and coleoid cephalopods using rapid, snapping bites.
Besanosaurus had large coronoid processes and rough surangulars that would have anchored strong jaw musculature.
Besanosaurus could not support a powerful bite, but its thin jaws allowed for rapid closing.
Besanosaurus likely swam using an eel-like motion by undulating its entire flexible body from side to side.
Besanosaurus had predominantly single-headed ribs which resulted in a flexible body, unlike double-headed ribs found in other ichthyosaurs.
Besanosaurus likely swam by undulating its body like an eel, suggesting modest speed but capable of rapid acceleration and good maneuverability.
Researchers suggest large size in Besanosaurus allowed for diverse feeding techniques, acted as an anti-predator adaptation, and improved thermoregulation.
Besanosaurus was a carnivore that primarily ate small fish, cephalopods, and other marine reptiles.

Some researchers debated whether the vertebrae found in the holotype were embryos or stomach contents of an immature mixosaurid, noting the vertebrae were the right size and more ossified than expected for an embryo.
Besanosaurus is generally classified as a shastasaurid, though its exact relationship to other members of the group remains unclear.
It is unclear exactly how Besanosaurus and other shastasaurid ichthyosaurs are related to one another.
Early phylogenetic analysis placed Besanosaurus in an intermediate position between the subfamilies Cymbospondylinae and Shastasaurinae.
Besanosaurus lived during the Middle Triassic, specifically the latest Anisian stage.
Besanosaurus dates to the latest Anisian and is the oldest definite shastasaurid genus.
Some researchers suggested in 1998 that Besanosaurus might represent another specimen of Shastasaurus, though it is generally accepted as a valid taxon.
Maisch argued in 2010 that Pessopteryx and Besanosaurus were not close relatives and showed various differences.
Maxwell and Kear agreed in 2013 that Pessopteryx was distinct from Besanosaurus, though they doubted some material assignments.
